title: Defect-Cavity Stack for Sharp Telecom Transmission Peak
scientific_hypothesis: Introducing a half-wave defect cavity within a Bragg reflector will create a narrow transmission peak at 1550 nm while maintaining high visible reflectance, because the defect creates a resonant mode within the photonic bandgap.
design_principle: A defect layer (typically half-wave optical thickness) breaks the periodicity of a Bragg stack, creating a localized resonant state that allows transmission at the defect wavelength while the surrounding Bragg mirrors maintain high reflectance elsewhere.
proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) x 5 | HfO2 (defect) | (SiO2 | HfO2) x 5 | Fused Silica substrate (21 layers total: 10 pairs plus one defect layer)
design_variables: Defect layer position within the stack
Thicknesses of the surrounding Bragg mirror pairs
soft_objectives: Maximize transmittance peak at 1550 nm center of telecom band
Minimize transmission bandwidth to reduce out-of-band leakage
manufacturing_considerations: 21 layers uses 70 percent of the 30-layer budget
Defect thickness control is critical for peak wavelength accuracy
HfO2/SiO2 defect cavities have been demonstrated in high-power laser applications per L09, L15
theory_basis: Defect mode theory in 1D photonic crystals
Cavity resonance in distributed Bragg reflectors
expected_advantages: Very sharp transmission peak at telecom wavelength
Excellent visible rejection from strong Bragg mirrors
Defect position provides additional design degree of freedom
known_risks: Transmission peak may be too narrow for full 1530-1565 nm band
Defect layer thickness tolerance is critical
May require more mirror pairs to achieve sufficient visible reflectance
execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer defect-cavity stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: 5 HfO2/SiO2 (Lemarchand) pairs, then one HfO2 defect layer, then 5 SiO2 (Lemarchand)/HfO2 pairs (mirror symmetry around defect). Optimize defect layer thickness to center transmission peak at 1550 nm, and optimize surrounding mirror pair thicknesses for maximum visible reflectance. Initial defect thickness set to half-wave optical thickness at 1550 nm. Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from catalog. Substrate: SiO2 (Lemarchand) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light.
